Distinct native-lowering bug, untouched by the transport arc. IMPORTANT: the transport LAYER for these is now fixed (the f98.14 unit tests pass), but the END-TO-END matrix fixtures fail on DOWNSTREAM native codegen — separate bug.
- enum_take_drop_split: Cranelift arg-count mismatch (return_call fn6: got 4 expected 5) on run/build; 'ambiguous across callable entries' on interp. Different bug from the transport arc.
- actor_ring::interp: 'backend callable 66 ... has no settled callable entry', deterministic.
- enumerable_protocol_dispatch.fz (fz-bv3, DIVERGED from membership_operator which is now fixed): 'missed an exhaustive dispatch' on all paths.
- return_widening_shard_1: REAL budget regression ('corpus max return ascents grew to 6' — RETURN_WIDENING_BUDGET headroom). Belongs to the .28.6/.40 widening family, NOT a flake.
- exhaustiveness-diagnostic family (fz-9i4.7.1): spec_violation, case_tuple_pattern_sequential, tree (tree also overshoots scalar_box_allocs by 14). keyword_lists (fz-9i4.7.6, echo/2 unbound). resource_lifecycle (fz-9i4.7.5). enum_reduce_suspend (fz-hwn.13). enum_list_allocations/enum_sort interp telemetry drift (fz-rh2.16.2). fz_f98 crashes (range_reduce2/enum_tier0/map_reduce). enum_map_family build/run wrong numeric results (interp already passed). sample_tests* ('test fixtures' unimplemented — out of scope).

- repr_seam_enum_count_after_reduce2::interp: flips between 10/10 (5/10) and 2/2 (5/10), NEVER the correct 10/2 — a duplication/aliasing bug (demand-cone membership variance), always wrong. Needs a fix, not a re-run policy.

STALE-ORACLE CAVEAT (do NOT blindly re-bless): append/quicksort/reverse fail on reductions_remaining metadata ONLY (stdout matches), by NON-UNIFORM deltas (append 1, reverse 2, quicksort 28). Per CLAUDE.md this is a real signal (extra reduction-accounting work), not stale goldens — trace the delta source before touching the goldens.

NEW TICKET FILED: AOT resource-dtor teardown SIGBUS (a-resource_aot_dtor/file_handle/file_resource_lifecycle ::build — build ok, correct output, then SIGBUS at teardown; sibling of fz-9i4.7.5). native.rs:3123 panic still belongs in this bucket. The f98.14 AOT-grind item is now split: transport unit tests FIXED, end-to-end fixtures still red on downstream codegen.

comments.text: CORRELATION (fz-go4.18.22 diagnosis, 2026-07-02): the matrix redness on this machine IS (near-totally) the oscillation family. Census with a per-key value-history detector: 215 cycling re-productions across the matrix sweep, 100% RuntimeDemand keys, 9 fixtures — enum_predicate_search(84), fz_f98_range_reduce_scalar(48), opaque_fn_value_join(26), map_enumerable(20), enum_map_family(10), tailcall_closure_captures(9), repr_seam_enum_count_after_reduce2(6), range_enumerable(6), native_tuple_accumulator_tail(6) — overlap with the ~22 drifting matrix failures near-total. Also proven: the cycling fixtures' PRODUCTS are not schedule-deterministic (3-run fingerprint diffs on the Enum.reduce/reverse cone), i.e. the stale-oracle failures (3934 vs 3906 reduction pins etc.) are plausibly the compiler shipping schedule-dependent products, NOT stale goldens. TRIAGE THIS TICKET AFTER fz-go4.18.22's fix lands — most of it should collapse; whatever remains is genuinely stale oracles / the AOT-grind family.

Dep added: blocked by fz-go4.18.22 (the census proved the matrix redness is near-totally the RuntimeDemand cycling family; triage AFTER the redesign lands — most should collapse; what remains is genuinely stale oracles / the AOT-grind family).

F2 EVIDENCE (from the fz-go4.18.22 rework): fixtures2/behavior/repr_seam_enum_count_after_reduce2 is NOT a deterministic moved miscompile — it is a pre-existing SCHEDULE-DEPENDENT one, unchanged by 18.22 and by its F1 rework. 10-run interp distributions: parent f92375bc6 = 8x'10,10' / 2x'2,2'; 0810fcb89 = 6x'10,10' / 4x'2,2'; F1-fixed = both shapes too. Expected '10,2'; both wrong shapes print ONE closure-call's result for BOTH dbg callsites (reduce reducer vs count predicate conflated at a callable seam; which side wins is a coin flip). The backend program differs on EVERY run of the SAME build (4 runs -> 4 distinct dumps: generated FunctionIds 161/162 swap, transport position orderings churn) — fz-go4.18.21's schedule-dependent arrow keying territory. The JIT path fails identically and deterministically on all three commits: 'codegen: native callable value Var(3) has no settled callable boundary' (fz-f98.14 family). RuntimeDemand itself is clean on this fixture on both 0810fcb89 and the rework: 3 productions, 0 identical re-productions, and the rework's stale-caller re-settle loop never fires on it — the residual is downstream of demand.

Census result (fz-go4.18.28): the AOT-grind bucket IS the transport per-anchor global re-solve — keystone fix filed as fz-go4.18.28.1 (expected: 00420 >30min -> seconds). Triage this ticket after fz-go4.18.28.1 lands. Also noted by the census: 143/556 fixtures exit nonzero under RAW interp (no matrix defer/annotation context) — not a defect count per se, but worth a pass when triaging.

PARALLEL-FLAKE DATA POINT (from fz-yj0 verification, 2026-07-06; fz-4zs closed as dup of this + fz-0lm): 'cargo test --test fixture_matrix' in DEFAULT parallel mode gave 27, then 21, then (single-threaded) 19 failures across consecutive no-change runs, with DIFFERENT names appearing/disappearing (curried_add, defstruct_runtime, destructure_*). Same 3s-build-timeout-under-contention family already noted here + the fz-0lm concurrent-AOT-output race. OPERATIONAL GATE that works today: 'cargo test --test fixture_matrix -- --test-threads=1' is deterministic and yields the stable 19-known-red baseline; any 'fixture stays exactly N' regression check MUST be single-threaded until the timeout/race fixes (this ticket + fz-0lm) land.

CI-coverage data point (PR 83 run 32504237709): with enum_map_family newly undeferred (fz-9i4.7.10.2), its run lane joins the CI timeout family -- interp and build lanes pass in CI, run exceeds its 15s budget under cargo-llvm-cov instrumentation + parallel workspace contention (locally: 8.8s debug, all three lanes green).
